intro.title: Build confirmation dialog service
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable confirmation dialog service in JavaScript. You will create a function that displays a modal dialog to ask users for confirmation before proceeding with an action, such as deleting an item. The core concept is using JavaScript functions and DOM manipulation to dynamically show and hide dialog elements on a webpage. You will work with HTML elements, event listeners, and callback functions to handle user responses. This service helps improve user experience by preventing accidental actions in web applications.
intro.usecase: Confirmation dialogs are essential in production applications to prevent accidental data loss or irreversible actions. You'll see them in e-commerce platforms when removing items from a cart, in admin dashboards before deleting user accounts, and in content management systems when publishing or discarding draft changes. As a developer, implementing a reusable confirmation service ensures consistent user experience across your application while reducing code duplication. This pattern is particularly valuable in complex interfaces where users frequently perform destructive operations like bulk deletions, payment confirmations, or system configuration changes.
